chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who borrows money and performs Hajj, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has wealth left behind, and if death were to befall him, it would be paid off from him, so there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to borrow money to perform Hajj if one has assets to cover the debt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that borrowing for Hajj is permissible provided the debtor leaves sufficient assets to settle the debt, ensuring the obligation is not neglected. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on balancing spiritual aspiration with financial responsibility, distinguishing between valid debt and neglect of obligation. The condition reflects the broader principle that Hajj is a duty, not a license for financial irresponsibility.
